17. We now proceed to examine the submissions of the Petitioner to arrive at the

Asset-7 as on 1.4.2019 (including Initial Spares of ₹ 510.18 lakh) consists of trued-
up capital cost of ₹ 8030.32 lakh (including Initial Spares allowed of ₹497.87) as on
31.3.2019 and ₹ 12.31 lakh of additional Initial Spares (which were allowed based on
the APTEL Judgment dated 14.9.2019).
19. For arriving at the opening capital cost as on 1.4.2019 for truing-up of the
tariff, only parameter which needs to be checked is the allowable limit of Initial
Spares since IDC and IEDC accrued till CODs of all assets were discharged before
31.3.2019 and are already a part of the trued-up capital cost of ₹ 8830.32 lakh as on
31.3.2019.

24. ACE claimed for the financial year 2019-20 is ₹189.19 lakh on combined
basis. As per Liability Flow Statement for each asset as submitted by the Petitioner,
the liabilities recognized as on 31.3.2019 on combined basis is ₹189.19 lakh, i.e.,
equal to the ACE claimed. As such, all the previous liabilities existing as on
31.3.2019 have been discharged in the financial year 2019-20. As per Auditor
Certificates, liquidated damages of ₹ 29.83 lakh (including ₹ 27.13 for Asset-4) were
received in 2019-20. The Petitioner has submitted that since IDC and IEDC to the
tune of ₹19.14 lakh was deducted on COD on account of time overrun not allowed in
commissioning of Asset-4 and discharge of ₹ 1.79 lakh is not allowable as the limit of

allowable Initial Spares has already been exhausted, the combined ACE claimed of
₹189.19 lakh, has been arrived at by i) adding back LD to the extent of IDC and
IEDC deducted due to time overrun, i.e., ₹ 19.14 lakh and by ii) subtracting excess
Initial Spares of ₹ 1.79 lakh from the Auditor certified expenditure of ₹ 171.84 lakh for
the financial year 2019-20. Further, it is noted that Auditor Certificates indicate that
the expenditure is net of Liquidated Damages. Implicitly, the gross expenditure due
to discharges is ₹ 201.67 lakh (171.84+29.83) and since all liabilities have been
discharged, the liabilities before adjustments of LD and excess Initial Spares, is ₹
201.67 lakh.
25. It is noted that for Asset-2 and Asset-4, the ACE claimed is ₹ 73.48 lakh
(14.13+59.36), for the financial year 2019-20 and the same is claimed under
Regulation 25(1)(a), i.e., expenditure incurred on “Liabilities to meet award of
arbitration or for compliance of the directions or order of any statutory authority, or
order or decree of any court of law”. However, we find that there is no mention of any
arbitration/court order in the Petition.
26. We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner. The treatment of LD
received, i.e., reducing it from the gross ACE for the year in which LD is received
and then adding back LD to the extent of IDC and IEDC deducted due to time
overrun to arrive at the ACE claimed for the year, is in line with the practice adopted
in earlier truing up Orders.
27. Accordingly, Petitioner has claimed ACE during the FY 2019-20 as Rs.189.19
lakh for the Combined Asset. On individual Assets’ basis, the ACE claim

amounts to ₹ 115.71 lakh and for Asset- 2, and Asset- 4 under the Regulation
25(1)(a) amounting to ₹ 73.48 lakh.
28. As per the Liability Flow Statements for Asset-1, Asset- 3 and Asset-7, as
submitted by the Petitioner, the liabilities recognized as on 31.3.2019 are ₹ 115.71
lakh, which have been discharged in the financial year 2019-20. These are approved
as ACE against the said three Assets under Regulation 25(1)(d).
29. ACE claim of ₹ 73.48 lakh against Asset-2 and Asset- 4 under Regulation
25(1)(a) are on account of expenditure incurred on liabilities to meet award of
arbitration or for compliance of the directions or Order of any statutory authority, or
Order or Decree of any court of law; Arbitration/court order details were provided
neither in the current Petition nor in the 2014-19 True up Petition. Vide TV letter
dated 31.7.2025, the Petitioner was directed to provide the details of the works for
Add-cap claimed under Regulation 25(1)(a) and 25(1)(d).
30. In response, the Petitioner has preferred not to furnish any
information/explanation pertaining to the Add-cap claimed under Regulation 25(1)(a).
We acquiesce that there is no Arbitration /Court Order. Consequently, we are not
inclined to allow the ACE ₹ 73.48 lakh claimed for Asset- 2 and Asset- 4 under the
Regulation 25(1)(a). Accordingly, ACE for Asset- 2 and Asset- 4 under Regulation
25(1)(a) is ‘Nil’.
31. Hence, the ACE Approved for the Combined Asset is ₹ 115.71 lakh during the
FY 2019-20.
